scenes.heading: Cache Invalidation
scenes.narration: Dispatcher. Cache Invalidation. In this video we review 8 key concepts you need to know for the certification.

scenes.question: How does Dispatcher mark cached content as invalid after activation?
scenes.heading: Dispatcher invalidates cached files by touching a .stat file
scenes.body: The speech says Dispatcher invalidates files by touching a .stat file and then compares that file's modification date with the cached document's modification date.
scenes.narration: How does Dispatcher mark cached content as invalid after activation? Dispatcher invalidates cached files by touching a .stat file. The speech says Dispatcher invalidates files by touching a .stat file and then compares that file's modification date with the cached document's modification date.

scenes.question: What does /statfileslevel control in Dispatcher cache invalidation?
scenes.heading: /statfileslevel limits .stat touching to the docroot-to-resource path depth
scenes.body: The speech explains that /statfileslevel controls how many folder levels get a .stat file and that only .stat files from docroot down to the file's level, or the configured depth, are touched.
scenes.narration: What does /statfileslevel control in Dispatcher cache invalidation? /statfileslevel limits .stat touching to the docroot-to-resource path depth. The speech explains that /statfileslevel controls how many folder levels get a .stat file and that only .stat files from docroot down to the file's level, or the configured depth, are touched.

scenes.question: A team configured a custom /statfile name, but Dispatcher still uses .stat files. Why?
scenes.heading: When /statfileslevel is set, Dispatcher ignores /statfile and uses .stat
scenes.body: The source says that if /statfileslevel is set, the /statfile property is ignored and .stat is used.

scenes.question: What happens to auto-invalidated files defined by /invalidate?
scenes.heading: Auto-invalidated files stay on disk and are revalidated on the next request
scenes.body: The speech says auto-invalidated files are not deleted right away; their validity is checked at the next request.
scenes.narration: What happens to auto-invalidated files defined by /invalidate? Auto-invalidated files stay on disk and are revalidated on the next request. The speech says auto-invalidated files are not deleted right away; their validity is checked at the next request.

scenes.question: Which pattern is typically used in /invalidate for linked page content?
scenes.heading: A common /invalidate setup denies everything and allows *.html
scenes.body: The speech says /invalidate is typically used for HTML pages because pages link to each other, and the usual configuration denies everything and allows *.html.

scenes.question: What is required for a manual Dispatcher flush request?
scenes.heading: A manual flush is an HTTP POST to /dispatcher/invalidate.cache with CQ-Action and CQ-Handle
scenes.body: The speech defines a manual flush as an HTTP POST to /dispatcher/invalidate.cache with headers including CQ-Action and CQ-Handle.

scenes.question: Which header value should be used when only the targeted resource should be flushed without invalidating other cache areas?
scenes.heading: CQ-Action-Scope: ResourceOnly flushes only the targeted resource
scenes.body: The speech states that the header CQ-Action-Scope with value ResourceOnly flushes a resource without invalidating other parts of the cache.

CQ-Action-Scope: ResourceOnly flushes only the targeted resource. scenes.question: Why is defining /allowedClients recommended in the cache section?
scenes.heading: Without /allowedClients, any client can clear the cache
scenes.body: The speech recommends defining /allowedClients because, if it is not defined, any client can clear the cache and repeated flushes can severely hurt performance.
